products.name: Azimutt
products.description: Database explorer and analyzer for large/complex schemas. Offers visual schema exploration, data exploration, database analysis with rule-based optimization suggestions, and collaborative documentation via AML (Azimutt Markup Language) diagrams.
products.positioning: Exploration-first tool for large monolithic or microservice databases; targets DevOps, data analysts, and teams needing operational schema documentation.

products.name: ChartDB
products.description: AI-powered database schema visualization tool with instant SQL import (~15 seconds), real-time collaboration, live database sync, and smart query-based schema extraction. Supports multiple relational databases.
products.positioning: Fast, visual, cloud-first ERD tool for teams; emphasizes speed of import and AI-assisted schema design over deep exploration.

products.name: dbdiagram.io
products.description: Code-first database diagram tool using DBML (Database Markup Language) DSL. Emphasizes simple, text-based schema definition with visual preview, SQL import, and basic collaboration features.
products.positioning: Minimalist, code-first approach for developers who prefer text-based versioning over visual design; tight integration with Git workflows.

products.name: DrawSQL
products.description: Visual database schema diagram tool with real-time collaborative editing, AI schema review (indexes, naming conventions), and architecture-review ready presentation. Includes discussion threads on canvas and version history.
products.positioning: Design-focused, collaborative ERD tool for teams running architecture reviews; strong HCI for visual design and discussion workflows.

products.name: DbSchema
products.description: All-in-one database design and management tool with visual reverse engineering, ERD creation, data exploration, SQL client, and Git integration. Supports 100+ databases with offline design capability and deployment-safe schema migration workflows.
products.positioning: Enterprise/team-focused tool for DBAs, architects, and developers; emphasizes comprehensive feature set (design → document → deploy) with visual-first no-SQL-required interface.

products.name: Prisma Studio
products.description: Visual database browser and data editor integrated into Prisma ORM ecosystem. Provides no-SQL-required data exploration, filtering, search, and real-time team collaboration via Prisma Console. Focused on data browsing rather than schema design.
products.positioning: Developer tool within Prisma ecosystem; emphasizes data browsing and team collaboration over schema design; usage-based pricing tied to Prisma Postgres operations.

products.name: ER Flow
products.description: Modern online ER diagram tool with real-time collaboration, CRDT-powered sync, automatic SQL migration generation, and MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for AI coding assistant integration. Supports visual ER design with checkpoints/versioning.
products.positioning: AI-forward ER design tool for developers; emphasizes MCP integration for natural-language schema generation and modern collab features (CRDT sync, real-time cursors).

notes:
**Extraction completed for Phase C (EXTRACTION) – competitors-db-schema-modeling-visual leaf. **Coverage: 7 primary products (Azimutt, ChartDB, dbdiagram.io, DrawSQL, DbSchema, Prisma Studio, ER Flow) with systematic evidence from 59 T0/T1/T2/T3 sources across product pages, docs, GitHub, reviews, and vendor comparisons.**Product data:** All 7 products mapped to existing or new company stubs. Archetype, positioning, deployment, open-source status, and tech stack extracted from official pages and GitHub.

**Feature scoring (15-35 most relevant per product):**
- Azimutt: 14 features scored (schema introspection, data exploration, versioning, collaboration, deployment) – emphasis on large-schema exploration.
- ChartDB: 13 features scored (ERD, AI schema generation, instant import, collaboration, templates) – emphasis on speed and AI copilot.
- dbdiagram.io: 7 features scored (DBML editor, Git versioning, simple UX, limited collab) – code-first positioning.
- DrawSQL: 13 features scored (ERD design, multiplayer collab, AI review, templates, embedding) – collaboration and architecture review focus.
- DbSchema: 13 features scored (ERD, reverse engineering, data browser/editor, SQL client, Git, versioning) – all-in-one IDE positioning.
- Prisma Studio: 10 features scored (data browser, data editor, real-time collab, ORM integration, themes) – data-browsing focus within Prisma ecosystem.
- ER Flow: 10 features scored (ERD, AI MCP integration, real-time collab, comments, migration generation) – modern AI-first positioning.

**Competitor positioning:**
- **Direct (high threat): Azimutt, ChartDB, DrawSQL, ER Flow** – All offer visual ERD design, real-time collab, and/or AI features. Wedges: MetroGraph differentiates on orchestration graph design (control flow, agent loops), AI agent builder (not just schema copilot), and runtime execution visualization.
- **Direct (medium threat): dbdiagram.io** – Code-first DSL appeals to Git-native developers; MetroGraph wedge is visual node-edge design for non-developers + workflow orchestration.
- **Adjacent (medium threat): DbSchema** – All-in-one database IDE; MetroGraph wedge is narrower (orchestration + agents, not full DB lifecycle).
- **Indirect (low threat): Prisma Studio** – Data browser within ORM; minimal workflow orchestration overlap.

**Moats identified:** Azimutt (database analysis rules + large-schema UX), ChartDB (smart query import + template library), dbdiagram.io (DBML DSL + Git community), DrawSQL (multiplayer canvas + threaded discussions), DbSchema (100+ DB support + comprehensive IDE), Prisma Studio (ORM ecosystem integration), ER Flow (MCP protocol + CRDT sync).

**Evidence quality:** Strong T0 (homepages, pricing, GitHub) and T1 (docs, changelogs) coverage. T2/T3 (reviews, comparisons) provide user sentiment and competitive framing but limited deep technical detail on HCI friction beyond surface claims.
